title: Digital Marketing Specialist at Highadvocacy
description:
HighAdvocacy is hiring its first marketing person. Your job is to take our website from where it is today to 10,000+ qualified monthly visitors in the next six months. Youll get there through earned channels: blog posts that rank on Google, a real LinkedIn cadence on the company page and on the founders personal one, Reddit and X threads where our buyers hang out, and one or two channels youll find by testing a handful. For the first 60 days, Piyush (our co-founder) works alongside you. Hell review drafts, help you build a point of view, and give real feedback. After that, you start making the channel calls. By month six, youre the marketing brain of the company and Piyush is reviewing your decisions, not making them. This is a full-time, in-office role in Ahmedabad. You report directly to Piyush. Theres no agency next to you, no senior marketer above you, and no playbook on a shared drive. The brand voice on the internet six months from now will largely be the one you ship. What youll actually be doing Write 2-4 blog posts a week. Useful enough to rank on Google, honest enough to share. Run a 5x/week LinkedIn cadence on the company page. Collaborate with Piyush on posts from his personal profile. Find 15-20 conversations a week on Reddit, X, and LinkedIn where our ICP is asking real questions. Reply like a human, not a brand account. Live inside Ahrefs, Google Search Console, and Plausible. Use them to debug whats working, not to confirm what you already believe. Test one new channel every month: a newsletter swap, a podcast appearance, a community partnership. Be honest about whether its worth continuing. Ship a short dashboard every Friday. What went out, what moved, what youre trying next. Build a small library of templates, post formats, and frameworks the next hire can pick up. What success looks like Well measure progress against these checkpoints together: 4 blog posts shipped; a LinkedIn cadence running 5x/week; 15+ thoughtful Reddit or X comments out in the wild. You've tested SEO, LinkedIn, Reddit, X, and one community channel. You bring a written recommendation on which 1-2 channels deserve 70% of your time, defended in a Friday review. 5,000 qualified monthly visitors; at least one channel running on autopilot, without Piyush reviewing every piece of output. 10,000 qualified monthly visitors. Compounding output across two channels. Youre making channel-level decisions with light founder review. How we think about AI in this role We expect you to use AI every day. The difference we care about is using it as leverage versus using it as a crutch. Heres how we actually use these tools: Claude or ChatGPT - Drafting blog outlines, ideating angles, rewriting weak sections, testing your thinking, summarizing competitor content. Perplexity - Fast research, finding sources and statistics, sanity-checking claims before publishing. Ahrefs AI features - Keyword clustering, content gap analysis, surfacing backlink prospects. AI for repurposing - Turning one blog into a LinkedIn post, an X thread, and a Reddit reply, without making them sound like the same recycled paragraph. Pattern analysis - Pulling apart top-performing posts in our space and figuring out what's actually working. Cursor or v0 (bonus) - Spinning up small landing page experiments without waiting on a designer. What we dont want: AI-generated final copy anyone can spot in three seconds. Your taste and voice ship the final draft. AI gets you to about 60% of the work, faster. The last 40%, the part that makes it sound human, is on you. Who we're hoping applies The best signal for this role isn't years of experience or a degree. It's whether you live on the internet and pay attention to how things land. This role is probably right for you if a few of these are true: Youve drafted a LinkedIn post or a tweet in your head while showering. You can name 5 people you follow on X and explain why for each. You read the comments under good LinkedIn posts to figure out why they worked. Youd rather ship 50 honest LinkedIn posts than 1 polished case study that took a month to approve. You think most B2B SaaS marketing reads like the same paragraph copy-pasted across the internet, and you can point at examples. Youve shipped something publicly on your own time: a blog, an X account, a side project, a newsletter. Audience size doesnt matter. The shipping does. You use AI to move faster through the boring parts, not to think for you. Who probably shouldnt apply Skip this role if any of these feel true: You need a playbook handed to you before you can start. The first thing on your resume is HubSpot Certified or a marketing degree. You havent shipped anything publicly outside a job you were paid for. You find Ahrefs intimidating and dont want to learn it. You're hoping someone else (an agency, a senior, the founder) does the work and you review it. What we're not asking for None of these are required. Don't filter yourself out if you don't have them: Prior B2B SaaS experience. You'll pick up the context in two weeks. SEO certifications. Ahrefs and a few good blogs will teach you more in a month. Paid ads experience. Out of scope for this role. Video or design skills. Not what we need here. HubSpot, Marketo, or any specific automation tool. We dont use them.

title: Senior Marketing Manager
description:
About FIAB Finance in a Box is an accounting and financial consulting firm based in California, providing outsourced CFO and controller services to companies around the world. FIAB operates as one managed operating partner for finance, HR, and regulatory readiness for growing businesses. FIAB recently expanded beyond finance into HR services through its partnership with GyroHR, and is preparing to launch FinOpz, an AI-enabled finance operations platform, as a new product line alongside its core services business. 
 The Role Were looking for a Senior Marketing Manager / Marketing Lead to build and run marketing for Finance in a Box, as a hands-on, individual-contributor role working closely with FIABs fractional CMO. Youll personally plan, write, run, and measure campaigns, own the marketing side of our CRM (HubSpot), lead nurture campaigns, build our LinkedIn and thought-leadership presence, and work side-by-side with BD/Sales to turn marketing activity into a measurable pipeline. Youll also take on product marketing support for FinOpz, our new AI-enabled finance operations platform, as one part of a broader, all-around marketing role rather than a dedicated product marketing seat. Youll meet weekly with the fractional CMO to set priorities and review work, and use freelancers or agencies as extra hands, not as a substitute for your own execution. 
 Responsibilities Campaigns demand generation Own multi-channel campaign execution (LinkedIn, email, content, webinars/events) that generates qualified leads for priority segments. Manage the marketing side of our CRM (HubSpot): email nurture campaigns, list segmentation, and reporting, in coordination with BD/Sales on lead handoff and pipeline feedback. Partner with BD/Sales on account-based approaches for target accounts and joint go-to-market plans. Track leads through the funnel and report results and ROI to leadership. Brand content Build and personally drive our LinkedIn presence and thought-leadership content: founder posts, articles, case studies, and market commentary that build credibility across finance and HR/people-ops circles. Translate FIABs finance, HR, and expanding service offerings into clear, differentiated positioning and messaging for different buyer personas. Own website updates, one-pagers, decks, and sales-enablement content, working with leadership and BD. Track competitor positioning and market developments in fintech/finops, and B2B services to keep messaging sharp and current. Product marketing (FinOpz) Take on product marketing support for FinOpz as it moves through beta and toward public launch, coordinating with the fractional CMO on strategy and priorities. Process vendor management Build repeatable marketing processes, calendars, SOPs, and playbooks, proactively identifying and fixing gaps rather than running campaigns ad hoc. Brief and manage external agencies, freelancers, or contract designers/copywriters, holding them accountable for quality and deadlines while retaining ownership of strategy and outcomes. Meet weekly with the fractional CMO to set priorities, review work, and course-correct. 
 What Youll Need 10-12+ years of B2B marketing experience, with a strong track record in demand generation, not just brand or communications. Genuinely fluent with AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) as a core part of how you work, not an occasional add-on. Youll be a team of one and need to multiply your own output. Hands-on experience running the marketing side of a CRM/marketing automation platform (HubSpot strongly preferred): nurture tracks, list management, and reporting. Proven experience building LinkedIn presence and thought-leadership content for a B2B brand or leader. Experience working closely with BD/Sales on pipeline generation, lead handoff, and account-based approaches. Comfortable marketing technology, recruitment/HR, or financial and professional-services offerings to sophisticated B2B buyers. A bias for personal execution: comfortable writing copy, building campaigns, and getting into the details rather than only directing others. Data-driven mindset: able to set up and read funnel metrics and adjust tactics based on results. Experience managing external agencies, freelancers, or contractors to deliver on brief and on time. Strong written communication skills in English, with real editorial judgment on what AI-assisted drafts still need before theyre ready to ship. A self-starter who takes a loose direction and turns it into a concrete plan, and builds process and structure proactively. 
 Nice to Have Experience marketing a new product launch, ideally in B2B SaaS or fintech. Experience as the first or sole marketing hire in a growing services or technology business. Familiarity with account-based marketing motions alongside demand generation. Comfort with design/no-code tools (Canva, basic Figma, website CMS) to move quickly without always relying on a designer. Exposure to both US and India B2B buyer contexts. Experience working alongside a fractional or outside CMO/marketing advisor. Required Skills Branding CRM BD experience HubSpot Marketing
